summary: Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Hokkaido University (circa 1973–1977). He held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (circa 1991–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (circa 2003–2019).

Toshinori Ochiai is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He served at Kacho Junior College (circa 1989–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (circa 1996–2018), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (circa 1996–2018).
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1929–1932). He later held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (circa 1949–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (circa 2003–2008). He was a visiting researcher at Toyo University (circa 2014–2018) and a postdoctoral researcher at Zhejiang University (circa 2019).

Toshio Nagahiro was a historian, archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He held positions at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (circa 1955–1968), and Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under his doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (circa 1953–1965), the University of Tokyo (circa 1965–1977), Chuo University (circa 1977–1987), and Hannan University.

Toshiya Unebe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. In 2009, he was attested as an Associate Professor in the Department of Indian Studies at Nagoya University.

Totsudo Kato worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Enryo Inoue, Seiran Ouchi, and Bankon Shimada, attending Oriental Hall, Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University. He later taught at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Tou-hui Fok was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (until 1966) and Otani University (1969). He was attested as a lecturer at The Chinese University of Hong Kong in 1981.

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his undergraduate and doctoral degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University and Osaka City University (from 1981 to 2010), and directed the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

Travis L. Smith works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and completed his PhD at Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley. He has held positions at Barnard College, University of Florida, and UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (circa 1946–1970) and lectured for the Buddhist Society.

Trijang Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under teachers including Pabongka Dechen Nyingpo and Khyenrab Yonten Gyatso. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, among numerous other disciples.
Trine Brox is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer. She was attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Copenhagen in 2026.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (circa 1938–1941). He held positions at Chatham University (circa 1944–1945), Parsons College (circa 1945–1946), University of Akron (circa 1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

Trulshik Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and taught prominent figures including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.
Trung Huynh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long, attested in 2016.
